title: What a simple kidney cyst is
text: A simple kidney cyst is a fluid-filled sac in or on a kidney. It is different from a solid stone or a solid mass. Confirmed simple cysts are usually benign and often found accidentally during imaging for another reason. The project's broad cyst label does not establish that a particular lesion is a simple cyst.

title: Simple cysts, complex lesions and cystic disease differ
text: The word cyst covers several situations: a simple fluid-filled cyst, a more complex cystic lesion, inherited polycystic kidney disease, or acquired cysts in chronic kidney disease. title: Possible symptoms and complications of a cyst
text: A cyst can occasionally cause side or back discomfort, press on nearby structures, bleed, become infected or interfere with urine flow. These are not the usual course of a simple cyst. New pain, fever or blood in urine needs assessment; do not automatically attribute it to a previously harmless cyst.

title: Polycystic kidney disease is not an ordinary simple cyst
text: Polycystic kidney disease, or PKD, is a genetic condition involving multiple kidney cysts. It can enlarge the kidneys, affect kidney function and cause problems outside the kidneys. title: PKD and pregnancy planning
text: PKD with high blood pressure or reduced kidney function can complicate pregnancy. Discuss pregnancy plans early with the kidney and maternity teams, including a review of medicines. Do not independently start or stop treatment from generic advice.

title: Diet and fluid advice in PKD

title: Acquired cysts in chronic kidney disease
text: Acquired cystic kidney disease develops in people who already have chronic kidney disease or kidney failure. It is different from inherited PKD. It becomes more common with longer-standing kidney failure; dialysis itself is not considered the cause of the cysts.
